identity.name: Hetta Cole
identity.culture: capital artisan's quarter; her grandmother's forge
identity.occupation: Smith and artisan; tools, hinges, buckles, repairs

publicReputation.value: The smith who fixes anything and talks about as much as the anvil does.

privateReality.value: She recognizes the realms' craftsmanship on sight — she has re-set their heating charms for Joren Pell — and she watches the hero snap work she admires into 'shards'.

primaryDesire.value: To make things that hold — and, lately, to quietly repair as much of the realms' broken domestic magic as reaches her bench.

primaryFear.value: That the hero will one day bring her a shard to 'reforge into a weapon' and she will have to decide what kind of smith she is.

centralValue.value: Judge the work, not the worker. Good joinery is good joinery whoever poured it.

mainFlaw.value: She says everything through the work and almost nothing with her mouth, so the hero has never once understood her.

centralContradiction.value: Her craft teaches her that the realms' artisans are excellent — and her customer is the man breaking their work for kindling.

moralBoundary.value: She will not unmake: no reforging a charm into a blade, no sharpening what was built to warm or feed.

breakingPoint.value: The day he actually asks — sets a memorial-lamp fragment on her anvil and says 'make it kill better'.

opinions.reason: He breaks excellent work and calls the pieces evil; she has repaired what he breaks, so she knows exactly how good it was.
opinions.canChangeCondition: Escalates with run count: early she is simply curt; mid-arc she names the maker's technique of every piece he broke; late-arc she tells him what she re-set for Joren this month. Softens if he ever brings her something to fix, not break.

illustrativeLine.value: That 'dark shard' was a goblin hinge charm. Good work. Better than mine, some years. You snapped it with a boot.

opinions.reason: He sends her the broken pieces with the makers identified; the bench drawer of mended charms is their shared quiet resistance.
opinions.canChangeCondition: If the drawer is ever discovered, she takes the blame for both of them.

voice.rhythm: Sparse; speaks between hammer blows, and the hammer usually has the last word.

metaphorDomain.source: heat, temper, grain, joins, and the anvil

examples.value: Quench a blade too fast and it shatters. Same with people who only ever hit things.

sampleLines.value: Hinge charm. Goblin make, cold-set, no seam. You broke it in half. It was better work than yours.
I mend tools. I don't unmake them. Whatever you're about to ask, that's the answer.
The realms' smiths quench slow and stamp their work. I know four of their marks. You've brought me all four, in pieces.

antiSampleLines.value: For the hero's holy crusade, I shall forge a blade of legend!
Grr, smash good! Hetta like smash!

pressure.voiceShift: Down to single sentences; hammer fills the gaps.
pressure.behaviour: When he hears 'this was someone's heating charm' as 'corrupted artifice', she takes the piece off her anvil and puts it out of his reach.

illustrativeLine.value: Off the anvil. That one's going home mended, not back to you in halves.

pressure.voiceShift: Even fewer words; the work gets louder.
pressure.behaviour: Late-runs posture: she tells him, once per visit, what came through her drawer this month — then nothing else.

illustrativeLine.value: Re-set three heating stones this month. Yours broke them. That's the whole conversation.

pressure.voiceShift: No shift at all, which is the answer.
pressure.behaviour: Compliments about her craft land only if they come with work to do; praise of her 'service to the cause' gets the anvil.

illustrativeLine.value: Compliment's noted. It still needs a new haft. Six coppers.

notes: She KNOWS fact_shards_are_domestic_magic — she has physically re-set the realms' charms for Joren; this is the judgment call behind her whole profile. The 'mended charms drawer' is her and Joren's shared subplot; it is in her secrets-adjacent behavior (opinion not publicly admitted) but not in the `secrets` bucket because the schema tracks facts, and no fact covers the drawer. If a later agent adds a canon fact for it, wire it into `secrets`. She does not know the book is a comedy — she has never read it.
